basic_info.name: MedGemma (MedGemma 1 / MedGemma 1.5; Google Health AI Developer Foundations)
basic_info.description: MedGemma is Google's open-weights clinical model collection, built on Gemma 3 and trained for medical text and image comprehension, available as a 4B multimodal model, a 27B text-only model and a 27B multimodal model, plus Health AI Developer Foundations companions (MedSigLIP image encoder, MedASR medical speech-to-text). The re-check requested by this research item is negative on its central premise: as of 2026-09-16 there is still NO dedicated text-summarization variant. The newest release, MedGemma 1.5 4B (created 2026-01-13), adds medical document understanding (unstructured lab report PDF to structured JSON), improved text-based EHR interpretation, 3D/CT/MRI, whole-slide histopathology and longitudinal CXR support, and improved text reasoning - but it remains a general medical-comprehension foundation model that must be prompt-engineered or fine-tuned for note generation. The single most load-bearing fact for MediKiosk is that the model weights remain gated behind the non-permissive Health AI Developer Foundations (HAI-DEF) terms of use - not Apache-2.0 - which require accepting terms on Hugging Face, prohibit uses that could cause a health regulator to deem Google a medical-device manufacturer, and must be passed downstream as enforceable provisions. That, plus English-centric evaluation and the absence of any FHIR/NRCeS output, keeps MedGemma out of Module C as a runtime engine.
basic_info.organization: Google (Health AI Developer Foundations team; model built on Google DeepMind's Gemma 3)
basic_info.status: production - actively maintained developer model family; MedGemma 1.5 4B shipped 2026-01-13 and the model card was last updated 2026-04-21; MedGemma 1 (4B/27B) remains available under version 1.0.0

technical_features.what_it_does: MedGemma is a medical-domain generative model that reads medical text, medical documents and medical images and generates free text; it is presented by Google as a starting point that developers fine-tune or prompt-engineer for downstream tasks. Its documented use cases explicitly include patient interviewing, triaging, clinical decision support and summarization, and the model has been demonstrated to turn doctor-patient transcripts into SOAP-format notes. The 1.5 4B update materially improves the two capabilities closest to Module C: medical document understanding (extracting structured values and units from unstructured lab-report PDFs into JSON, macro F1 up to 91 on an internal dataset) and text-based EHR understanding (EHRQA accuracy up from 67.6 to 89.6, EHRNoteQA 80.4). It does not, however, produce FHIR or ABDM-conformant artifacts, does not do deterministic slot extraction or provenance, and has not been evaluated for multi-turn dialogue - so as a Module C engine it would only ever be the text-synthesis component behind an evaluation harness, never the contract emitter.
technical_features.architecture: Decoder-only Transformer, same architecture as Gemma 3, with grouped-query attention (GQA); multimodal variants add a SigLIP image encoder pre-trained on de-identified medical data (radiology, histopathology, ophthalmology, dermatology). The LLM component is trained on medical text, medical QA pairs, FHIR-based EHR data (27B multimodal only), 2D/3D radiology, histopathology, ophthalmology and dermatology images, and lab reports for document understanding. Context length at least 128K tokens; inputs normalized to 896x896 per image (256 tokens each); output capped at 8192 tokens. Training used JAX.
technical_features.inputs: Text prompts/questions, medical images (2D CXR/derm/fundus, CT/MRI volumes, whole-slide histopathology), medical documents (lab-report PDFs/images), and text-based electronic health record data. Multimodal variants accept image+text; the 27B text-only variant accepts text only. No structured dialogue-slot or FHIR input contract is defined.
technical_features.outputs: Generated free text only - answers, analyses, or a summary of a document; for the document-understanding task, structured JSON extracted from lab-report PDFs. There is no native FHIR Bundle, Composition, OPConsultRecord or NRCeS-profile output; any FHIR emission would be an external wrapper written by the developer.
technical_features.standards_compliance: None for the ABDM/NRCeS contract. MedGemma was trained on FHIR-based EHR data (27B multimodal) but does not emit FHIR, and no NRCeS FHIR IG, HL7 IPS or ABDM OPConsultRecord conformance is claimed or validated. Google's own FHIR/DICOM work is about feeding data into the model (Cloud Healthcare API, DICOM Store, Model Garden, MCP), not about producing conformant clinical documents. [NRCeS/FHIR emission: not applicable - uncertain that any is intended]
technical_features.offline_capability: The 4B model can be downloaded and executed entirely locally after the gated terms are accepted; Google describes MedGemma 1.5 4B as 'small enough to run offline', and the original release stated MedGemma 4B and MedSigLIP 'can even be adapted to run on mobile hardware'. Official examples run on a single GPU (bf16, device='cuda'); CPU execution is possible only through community GGUF quantizations (e.g. Q4_K_M ~2.3GB weights / ~3GB RAM) on llama.cpp/Ollama. There is no built-in local storage, encryption, sync or store-and-forward mechanism - MedGemma is a model, not an offline application stack. [Official CPU support for the 4B at kiosk scale: uncertain - demonstrated by community quantizations, not by Google's own tables]
technical_features.languages_supported: Primarily English. The model card states safety evaluations used mainly English-language prompts, and most benchmarks (MedQA, MedMCQA, MMLU Med, EHRQA) are English. AfriMed-QA (a 25-question African medical QA test set) was included, showing some non-English medical QA transfer (56.0 for 1.5 4B), but Hindi/Devanagari, Hinglish or any Indic-language clinical summarization is not officially benchmarked or claimed. [Hindi/Indic clinical quality: uncertain - not evidenced]
technical_features.deployment_model: Google positions MedGemma as a single-GPU model: 4B and MedSigLIP can be adapted to mobile hardware, while the 27B models generally need a GPU (Colab Enterprise advised to run 27B unquantized). Production/hosted deployment is via Google Cloud Vertex AI Model Garden with DICOM-aware and FHIR-aware options and MCP integration; the weights are also on Hugging Face (gated) and community GGUF packs exist for llama.cpp/Ollama. For MediKiosk's CPU/iGPU-only ~4GB kiosk, only the 4B class is even nominally relevant, and then only quantized; the 27B text model's Q4_K_M GGUF alone is ~16.5GB.

performance_metrics.accuracy_or_quality_metrics: Vendor-reported (MedGemma 1.5 4B unless noted): MedQA (4-op) 69.1, MedMCQA 59.8, PubMedQA 68.2, MMLU Med 69.6, MedXpertQA (text) 16.4, AfriMed-QA 56.0; text-based EHR: EHRQA 89.6 and EHRNoteQA 80.4 (versus 67.6 and 79.4 for MedGemma 1 4B); PDF-to-JSON lab extraction macro F1 91 (EHR Dataset 2), 71 (EHR Dataset 3), 85 (Mendeley PNG lab reports), 64 (EHR Dataset 4). The 27B text variant scores MedQA 85.3, MMLU Med 86.2, MedXpertQA 23.7. For clinical note generation specifically there is one community fine-tune (Tser-vak QLoRA on ACI-Bench + MTS-Dialog) reporting held-out ACI ROUGE-1 0.6227, ROUGE-2 0.3551, ROUGE-L 0.4239, BERTScore 0.8965, and the MEDIQA-OE-2025 team reported ~0.436 average for one-shot MedGemma 4B versus ~0.549 for 27B. A third-party reproducibility study found MedGemma 1.5 4B (BERTScore 0.848, judge 0.459, self-agreement 0.146, 28.7 tok/s) underperformed general Gemma 3 12B and Llama 3.1 8B - though that comparison is confounded by a 2-3x parameter gap. Base MedGemma 1 4B scored 64.4 on MedQA and, in an unblinded study, 81% of its chest X-ray reports were judged sufficient for similar patient management. Base MedGemma 27B text scored 87.7 on MedQA. All numbers are vendor-claimed or single-paper; none are peer-reviewed for note generation on Indian OPD data.
performance_metrics.latency: Google does not publish MedGemma latency tables. Third-party measured throughput: 28.7 tokens/s for MedGemma 1.5 4B in the reproducibility study (medium-varied hardware, not specified). No time-to-summary figures exist for CPU-only kiosk hardware. The 27B models are described as requiring a GPU (Colab Enterprise recommended). [Kiosk-CPU latency: uncertain - no published figure]
performance_metrics.resource_requirements: Model sizes: 4B multimodal (bf16 ~ several GB), 27B text-only and 27B multimodal (Colab Enterprise advised without quantization). Community 4B GGUF quantizations: IQ2_XS ~0.85GB / ~1.9GB RAM, Q2_K ~1.3GB / ~2.3GB RAM, Q4_K_M ~2.3GB / ~3GB RAM - i.e. the quantized 4B can fit the ~4GB kiosk budget, but at the cost of MedQA accuracy (56.0% at Q4_K_M, 34.7-43.8% at 2-bit). 27B text Q4_K_M is 16.5GB and Q2_K still 10.5GB, so the 27B variants are entirely out of budget. Official inference examples require a CUDA GPU in bf16.
performance_metrics.scale_metrics: No adoption or usage counts are published for MedGemma itself (Hugging Face download counts are not surfaced for the gated repos). The surrounding signals are substantive but not usage metrics: the MedGemma Impact Challenge on Kaggle, a growing Hugging Face collections page for MedGemma and for concept apps, a public GitHub repo with tutorial/fine-tuning notebooks, and adoption anecdotes from DeepHealth (US), Chang Gung Memorial Hospital (Taiwan) and Tap Health (Gurgaon, India - progress-note summarization and guideline nudges). Quantizations and fine-tunes exist on Hugging Face. [Install base / records processed: uncertain - none published]
performance_metrics.evaluation_protocol: Vendor benchmark evaluation: the MedGemma 1.5 model card and technical report (arXiv 2604.05081) report open plus internal datasets across imaging, text QA, medical-record QA and document-understanding tasks, with explicit data-contamination and single-image/no-multi-turn caveats. This is vendor-claimed baseline performance on English-centric benchmarks, not a peer-reviewed note-generation study. Independent evidence exists but is thin and mixed: a reproducibility study (arXiv 2604.10535) and a MEDIQA-OE-2025 order-extraction paper (arXiv 2511.10583), both preprint. For Module C, the usable protocol precedent is the community fine-tune's ACI-Bench/MTS-Dialog run (ROUGE/BERTScore) rather than any official MedGemma evaluation.

milestone_significance.relevance_to_module_c: MedGemma matters to Module C as the strongest clinically-specialized small open model and as the clearest example of 'medical grounding does not equal summarization readiness'. On the positive side it directly targets the right space - Google lists patient interviewing, triaging and summarization as use cases, the 1.5 4B update markedly improves medical-document and EHR comprehension (the exact Module B-to-C seam), and community work has already turned MedGemma into a dialogue-to-note model and a patient-friendly-summary teacher. On the negative side, the re-check this task asked for comes back empty: there is still no dedicated text-summarization variant, and the two hard blockers are unchanged - the weights are gated under non-permissive HAI-DEF terms that bar uses which could make Google a medical-device manufacturer, and the family remains English-centric with no Indic clinical evaluation. For a Ministry of Ayush/AIIA deployment, those facts mean MedGemma is not a candidate runtime engine; its value is (a) as a distillation teacher and (b) as a benchmark to beat on document understanding.
milestone_significance.what_to_adopt_or_reject: Adopt/adapt: (1) the teacher-model pattern - use MedGemma (or its 27B variant) offline during development to generate and judge training data, then distill into a permissively licensed student, exactly as the MedGemma Impact Challenge note-summarization project did (MedGemma-27B teacher to Gemma-2B student); (2) MedGemma 1.5's lab-report-PDF-to-structured-JSON capability as a reference target for Module B's document understanding, since it demonstrates realistic macro-F1 ceilings; (3) the disciplined framing that domain-adapted outputs are 'preliminary and require independent verification', which aligns with MediKiosk's physician-attestation posture. Reject: (1) shipping MedGemma weights as the kiosk runtime engine - the HAI-DEF license's medical-device clause and downstream-propagation obligation create exactly the kind of legal review friction a government-facing product should avoid, and Apache-2.0 alternatives (Gemma 4 E2B/E4B, Qwen3) remove that friction entirely; (2) the 27B variants - Q4_K_M alone is ~16.5GB; (3) any assumption that medical fine-tuning substitutes for summarization evaluation - the reproducibility and MEDIQA-OE results show a 4B clinical model can underperform a larger general model.
milestone_significance.limitations_and_risks: License and access: weights are gated on Hugging Face behind the HAI-DEF terms; distribution requires including the Section 3.2 restrictions as enforceable provisions, passing a copy of the agreement to recipients, and seeking Health Regulatory Authorization where applicable - and Google may remotely restrict usage. The terms forbid use that could make Google a medical-device manufacturer, which is a live concern for a physician-facing summary. Capability: no dedicated summarization variant; no multi-turn evaluation; explicitly not evaluated on multiple images; outputs 'not intended to directly inform clinical diagnosis, patient management decisions, treatment recommendations'; training may make it more prompt-sensitive than Gemma 3; data-contamination risk acknowledged. Language: English-centric evaluation, no Hindi/Indic clinical benchmark. Resource: only the 4B class fits ~4GB and only when quantized, with measurable accuracy loss at low bit-widths; 27B is out of scope. Evidential: no peer-reviewed note-generation evaluation and no Indian OPD validation, and a reproduction study found the 4B variant weakest on quality and consistency among compared models.
milestone_significance.differentiator_vs_medikiosk: MedGemma and MediKiosk barely overlap and do not compete. Object of work: MedGemma is a medical foundation model (text+image comprehension); MediKiosk's Module C is an elicitation-to-summary pipeline with a deterministic renderer and a validated FHIR output contract - the conversational HistoryBundle, per-field provenance and physician attestation are entirely absent from MedGemma. Output: MedGemma emits free text or extracted JSON, never NRCeS OPConsultRecord or any FHIR Bundle. License/runtime: MedGemma is gated, non-permissive and GPU-oriented, while MediKiosk's differentiation rests on offline-first CPU/iGPU operation, India data residency and validator-checked ABDM emission. Net effect: MedGemma does not erode any MediKiosk differentiator; if anything it strengthens the case for choosing an Apache-2.0 engine (Gemma 4 edge / Qwen3) and using MedGemma only as an offline training teacher or as a document-understanding reference point.

business_info.license: Non-permissive and gated. Model weights are governed by the Health AI Developer Foundations Terms of Use (license_name 'health-ai-developer-foundations' on Hugging Face), a custom agreement - not Apache-2.0 and not an OSI license. The agreement restricts use to the Prohibited Use Policy, forbids any use that could cause a health regulator to deem Google a medical-device manufacturer, requires downstream distribution of the restrictions as an enforceable provision plus a copy of the agreement, and lets Google remotely restrict usage it believes is in breach. Everything in the Google-Health/medgemma GitHub repository (not the weights) is Apache-2.0. Access requires a logged-in Hugging Face account that accepts the conditions.
business_info.pricing: No price for the model weights (free download subject to the HAI-DEF terms). Cost appears only when hosted: Google Cloud Vertex AI Model Garden dedicated endpoints and Cloud Healthcare/DICOM integration are paid Google Cloud services.
business_info.funding: Google-internal research and product effort (Health AI Developer Foundations / Google DeepMind); no external funding round, grant or investor is relevant.
business_info.commercial_status: Free developer model released by Google for research and product development; not sold as a product. Commercial use is permitted only within the HAI-DEF terms, which carry the medical-device-manufacturer restriction.

competition_ecosystem.competitors: General-purpose small models that can be fine-tuned for the same tasks (Gemma 4 E2B/E4B, Qwen3 small, Llama 3.x, Phi-4-mini, Mistral) are the practical alternatives because they carry permissive licenses. Medical-domain peers/alternatives include Med-PaLM/MedLM on Vertex AI, MedSigLIP (same family, imaging-only), BioMistral, OpenBioLLM and various MedQA-tuned community models. For the specific dialogue-to-note task the real comparators are the general models behind ambient scribes and the ACI-Bench/MTS-Dialog leaderboard systems, not other clinical LLMs.
competition_ecosystem.integrations: Google Cloud Vertex AI Model Garden (4B and 27B, 4-bit and 8-bit presets), Cloud Healthcare API DICOM Store and FHIR support, Model Context Protocol (MCP) for agentic pipelines, Hugging Face Transformers (Gemma 3 support from transformers 4.50.0) and community GGUF runtimes (llama.cpp/Ollama). Companion models: MedASR (medical speech-to-text) and MedSigLIP. Documented India-adjacent adopter anecdote: Tap Health (Gurgaon) summarizing progress notes.
competition_ecosystem.ecosystem_notes: The ecosystem signal is that clinical foundation models are being distributed under bespoke, gated, non-OSI terms while the general models underneath them (Gemma 4) have moved to Apache-2.0 - so the legal-friction gap now favours the general edge models for a government deployment. Google is also deliberately pushing MedGemma toward interoperability plumbing (DICOM/FHIR-aware deployment, MCP), which is useful context for Module B but does not make MedGemma a FHIR emitter. The MedGemma Impact Challenge has produced a body of community fine-tunes and distillation demos that MediKiosk can study as prior art for the eval-harness and teacher/student patterns.

history.release_date: MedGemma 1 initial release: 2025-05-20 (4B multimodal; 27B text-only). MedGemma 1 27B multimodal + MedSigLIP: 2025-07-09. MedGemma 1.5 4B: 2026-01-13. MedGemma 1.5 model card last updated 2026-04-21.
history.key_milestones: 2025-05-20 - MedGemma 1 4B multimodal and 27B text-only released (open, gated). 2025-07-09 - MedGemma 1 27B multimodal and MedSigLIP added; Google states all run on a single GPU and 4B/MedSigLIP can be adapted to mobile; a multimodal bug fix (missing end-of-image token). 2025-12-08 - Cloud integration hardened: DICOM-aware and FHIR-ready deployment options in Model Garden, MCP for agentic context. 2026-01-13 - MedGemma 1.5 4B released with 3D CT/MRI, whole-slide pathology, longitudinal CXR, bounding-box localization and improved medical-document/EHR understanding; MedASR released alongside; MedGemma Impact Challenge launched on Kaggle. 2026-04-21 - model card updated (last revised date on the 1.5 card).
history.recent_changes_last_6_months: Within the 2026-03-16 to 2026-09-16 window there is NO new MedGemma variant or text-summarization model: the last model release was MedGemma 1.5 4B on 2026-01-13 (outside the window) and the only in-window activity is documentation/benchmark housekeeping - the MedGemma 1.5 model card carries a 'last updated 2026-04-21'. The community side remained active in the window (new quantizations such as wredd/medgemma-4b-gguf for CPU, and fine-tunes such as Tser-vak/medgemma-4b-medical-note), and MedGemma-based preprint evaluations appeared (MedGemma 1.5 technical report arXiv 2604.05081; reproducibility study arXiv 2604.10535; MEDIQA-OE-2025 arXiv 2511.10583). The licence terms did not change in the window and remain the HAI-DEF terms. Net: the re-check for a text-summarization variant comes back negative. [Any unindexed release between 2026-04-21 and 2026-09-16: uncertain - none found]

market_positioning.target_users: Healthcare and life-sciences developers, applied ML researchers, and health systems building clinical AI applications; secondarily academic groups fine-tuning on medical data. Not aimed at patients or at clinicians as an end-user product.
market_positioning.market_segment: Medical/clinical foundation models and developer tooling for clinical AI - the model layer beneath ambient documentation, clinical decision support and imaging AI. It sits adjacent to, not inside, the intake/pre-consultation-summary or FHIR-tooling segments.
market_positioning.positioning_statement: Google positions MedGemma as the open model family that lets developers 'accelerate building healthcare-based AI applications' through strong baseline medical text and image comprehension, with the explicit instruction that it 'is a developer model that requires validation on the developer's intended use case' and that outputs 'should be considered preliminary and require independent verification, clinical correlation, and further investigation'. The 1.5 4B release is pitched as 'an ideal compute-efficient starting point... small enough to run offline', while the 27B models are for 'more complex text-based applications'.
